results.scenario: roommates discussing an unexpected living-room piano
results.trigger_note: A has already accepted an upright piano and scheduled its delivery for Saturday.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Aunt June has been clearing out the last things from her old house.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: She called because nobody else in the family has room for her upright piano.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I said I would measure our living room before getting back to her.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I told her we could take it, and the movers are bringing it here Saturday.

version_1.intended_interpretation: shock at the unexpected piano delivery
version_1.response: Wait, what? Did I misunderstand how much room you thought we had?

version_2.intended_interpretation: strong unwillingness to take the piano
version_2.response: Why not? It’s free, and I’ll clear the wall and move the bookcase myself before Saturday.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The gasp makes A stop and ask what surprising problem B has noticed, while the grunt reads as resistance to the piano itself and prompts A to argue for the plan and offer to handle the work.

results.scenario: roommates reviewing a landlord's carpet invoice
results.trigger_note: The landlord adds an absurd six-hundred-dollar charge labeled emotional support for the carpet.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I opened the envelope from the landlord about the hallway carpet.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I expected a normal cleaning charge after Juniper knocked over that plant.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: They itemized shampooing, deodorizer, and a replacement runner.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Then they added a six-hundred-dollar line called "emotional support for the carpet."

version_1.response: Wait, what does "emotional support for the carpet" even mean?

version_2.response: I know—apparently the carpet has feelings now, and they bill by the session.

results.why_the_vocalization_changes_the_respons: The gasp calls for A to stop and question the startling invoice charge, while the laughter invites A to joke along with the ridiculous wording.

shared_context.text: I was clearing out the hall cupboard to make room for the shoe rack.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Behind the bottom drawer, I found that little blue tin Mom used to keep on top of the fridge.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I thought it was full of loose buttons, because it disappeared when we packed up her kitchen.

shared_context.speaker: A

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: Every shelf had sticky jars, expired cans, and crumbs packed into the corners.

shared_context.speaker: A
shared_context.text: I finally pulled out the heavy bin on the bottom shelf to clean underneath it.

shared_context.speaker: A

shared_context.speaker: A

shared_context.speaker: A
